home.practice_cutting_blurb: Slice a slab of salvage along its grid and bank the pieces that hold one ore. Big pieces pay far more, and the cuts are few.
cutting.title: Cutting
cutting.how_to: A slab is made of blocks of ore with a few flaws in them. Swipe along a grid line to cut: the cut runs the whole way across the piece it is in and splits it in two. A piece that holds one ore only is banked at once for its size times its size, so one piece of twelve cells pays four times two of six. Each slab comes with a few cuts. When they are spent the rest is scrap, and the slab is graded against the best any plan could have made of it.
cutting.how_to_keyboard: Left and right move a cut that runs down, up and down move one that runs across, tab takes the next piece. Space or enter cuts, escape drops the cut, D gives the slab up.
cutting.tap_note: You can also tap near a line to see the cut, then tap it again to make it. A side that would be banked is ringed and shows what it pays.
cutting.grade_note: All of a slab's best is flawless, four fifths of it is clean. Flawless pays 100 and clean pays 40, times a streak of clean and flawless slabs that climbs to double. A rough slab breaks the streak.
cutting.hint_note: Practice rounds show a cut from a best plan when you pause. The first cut of a good plan often banks nothing.
cutting.legend_ores: Ores: each has a cut-out of its own. A flaw is a single cell of the wrong ore in a block.
cutting.legend_cut: A cut runs the whole way across the piece it is made in. A piece of one ore is banked for its size times its size; a mixed piece stays on the table.
cutting.legend_strip: Over the slab: a dot for each cut left, what you have banked against the slab's best with a notch where clean begins, and the chip that takes the next slab.
cutting.order_note: Each slab names an order: a plate of one size, either way round. A piece of exactly that size pays {bonus} more. Carve it only when that beats the bigger piece it comes out of.
cutting.legend_order: Beside the slab: the order, a plate of its size drawn to scale. A piece that would fill it is marked with a notch in each corner while the cut is lined up, and when it banks.
cutting.stage.blocks_intro: Pure blocks, and cuts enough for all of them. Free each big block whole: a piece pays its size times its size.
cutting.stage.flaws_intro: Flaws spoil blocks and there is a cut too few. Choose what to give up, and keep clean slabs coming for the streak.
cutting.stage.full_intro: Each slab names an order: a plate that pays more. Carve it when it beats the block it comes out of.
studio.preset.cutting_clean_blocks: Clean blocks: no flaws, every cut the slab needs
studio.preset.cutting_tight: Tight: cuts for two thirds of the slab
studio.preset.cutting_busy: Busy from the start: seven blocks, two flaws
studio.preset.cutting_big_slab: A big slab: eight by eight, up to nine cuts
